name: MARSHALL IS.
tagline: Atolls at the edge of sky

flag.title: Flag of the RMI
flag.note: Blue field, orange & white bands, 24-pt star

lead: The Marshall Islands are scattered across the Pacific like dropped beads. They are coral rings called atolls. The land is so flat that every view is ocean.
geo: Two chains, Ratak (Sunrise) and Ralik (Sunset), hold 29 atolls and 5 single islands. All 1,152 specks of land cover just 181 km². That is a little bigger than Washington D.C.
An atoll is a ring of reef around a sunken volcano. Kwajalein has the world's largest lagoon. The average height is just 2 metres, so high tides flood the land.
animals: More than 250 kinds of reef fish swim among 300 kinds of coral. Green and hawksbill sea turtles nest on quiet beaches.
The great frigatebird steals fish in mid-air. Giant coconut crabs climb palm trees and crack coconuts with claws like bolt cutters.
culture: Marshallese families follow the mother's side, so land and rank pass from mothers. Navigators used stick charts called rebbelib to read ocean swells.
Christmas, called Kūrijmōj, is a four-month party of songs and feasts. People still build outrigger canoes by hand.
history: Marshallese ancestors arrived about 2,000 years ago and mastered open-ocean sailing. Spain, Germany and Japan each claimed the atolls. The USA took over after World War II battles.
Between 1946 and 1958 the USA set off 67 nuclear bombs on Bikini and Enewetak. Their blast was 7,000 times the Hiroshima bomb. Independence came in 1986.
wows: Bikini Atoll is a World Heritage Site with sunken warships in its lagoon.
West of the Date Line, the islands share a day with Asia, not Hawaii.
Sailors felt ocean swells through the hull to find islands over the horizon.
The country uses the US dollar and has no central bank.
Bikini's soil has ten times more radiation than the Chernobyl and Fukushima zones.
Majuro's main island is under 300 metres wide.
Marshallese citizens can live and work in the USA without a visa.

myths.fact: Coconut palms and breadfruit trees grow thick, ringing blue lagoons.

myths.myth: Only Bikini islanders felt the nuclear tests
myths.fact: Fallout from the 1954 Castle Bravo test reached atolls about 150 km away.
